why: Sort, then compare neighbours: once sorted, a valid selection is a contiguous run where each value differs from the previous by at most 1, so the answer is the longest such run found in one pass.
hints: The condition is about neighbours in sorted order. What does the input look like after you sort it?
In the sorted array, a valid chain can always be taken as a contiguous run: skipping a value in the middle never helps.
Sort, then walk: extend the run while t[i] - t[i-1] <= 1, otherwise restart at 1. Track the longest run. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Duplicates are separate tickets and differ by 0, so they extend the run.
A single ticket is always a valid selection (answer >= 1).
